- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for the next 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts and forecasts a prolonged peak; reduce forecast slope after day 3–5 of spike.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and prices are falling, model frequently undercorrects; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days are above 75% of historical mean, forecast should be adjusted downward by 1–2% per day until mean reversion is observed.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period price movements (last 7–10 days); apply +0.5%–1.0% bias to final 7–10 days if sentiment is positive or neutral.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often fails to capture momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 3–5 days to adjust forecast direction.
